**Rooms sound like rooms.** Sounds now echo off the walls around you and
ring on in a tail measured from the map: corridors slap back, big metal halls
boom, wooden rooms stay dull and the outdoors is almost dry. The echoes come
from the direction of the walls that throw them back, and they fade smoothly
as you walk from one room into the next. The tail is kept a little dark and
lo-fi, like a late-90s 3D sound card. Music stays dry.

**Walls muffle, distance dulls.** Sounds you can't see come through muffled:
a little round a corner or through an open door, a lot behind closed doors
and solid walls. Far sounds lose their treble. Loudness stays exactly as in
vanilla DOOM, so you hear where monsters are just as well as before.

**A new Sound tab in F4.** Room acoustics, how loud the echoes are (25–200%),
muffling behind walls and dulling with distance can each be turned off or
tuned there.

**Cleaner mix.** Effects now use DOOM's real 0–15 volume scale and panning,
so the volume slider behaves as it should. A limiter briefly ducks the mix
during heavy gunfire instead of letting it crackle. On the Mac, General MIDI
music is 8 dB quieter so it sits under the effects.

**Uneven tiles.** Tiles, plates and stones painted into floors each lie a
little crooked, as if laid by hand. Lights catch some and miss others, and a
thin lip lights up or falls into shadow where neighbors meet. Panels and
bricks in walls and ceilings get the same treatment. They are two separate
F4 options, both on by default.

**Classic flashlight.** A new option, on by default: a shorter, warmer beam
that brightens what it hits in hard steps, like DOOM's own light levels, up to
a little past full brightness and no further. Monsters keep their palette
colors in the beam.

**Fast mouse turns fixed.** With uncapped frames, quick mouse flicks could
lose motion or snap the view the wrong way. Every frame's movement now counts,
and very fast flicks turn as far as they should.
